report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of session.py: Claim, TurnRef, ParticipantRecord, CouncilRecord dataclasses with docstrings. All docstring claims are checkable and kept.

handoff.purpose: Define Claim, TurnRef, ParticipantRecord, CouncilRecord dataclasses with docstrings and enforcement.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.note: Dataclass for one participant assertion; includes checkable flag and check string.

symbols.name: TurnRef
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for one chained turn with id, round, actor, status, etc.

symbols.name: ParticipantRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for roster accounting of one requested participant.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for council output; advisory by construction, no decision fields.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.checkable_claims
symbols.note: Property returning tuple of claims where checkable is True.

claims.text: ``checkable`` is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion.
claims.why: The Claim class has a checkable bool field and a check str field, consistent with the description.

claims.text: That is the council's entire product: a queue of checks for the gate to run.
claims.why: The code defines checkable_claims property on CouncilRecord, which returns a tuple of checkable claims; the class design supports this claim.

claims.text: A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own.
claims.why: Claim has verbatim field and checkable defaults to False; no scoring or weighting logic is present.

claims.text: There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object.
claims.why: CouncilRecord has no such fields; __post_init__ enforces advisory=True, preventing misuse.

claims.text: What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting.
claims.why: CouncilRecord contains claims (tuple of Claim), checkable_claims property, and participants tuple of ParticipantRecord.

claims.text: Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision.
claims.why: advisory defaults to True and __post_init__ raises ValueError if set to False.

claims.text: The queue the gate can actually run.
claims.why: Property filters claims where checkable is True, consistent with 'queue' concept.

observations.what: Claim class has fields author, vendor, model, round, role, text, cites, checkable, check, verbatim, parsed; all used as documented.
CouncilRecord has a __post_init__ that enforces advisory=True and ended in END_REASONS.
All dataclasses are defined with @dataclass or @dataclass(frozen=True) as appropriate.
No external references (e.g., END_REASONS, DEFAULT_TOKEN_CEILING) are defined in this chunk; their existence is assumed.
